subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw own failure-driven skill repair and usage-based skill retirement in core, expose a narrower plugin API for it, or leave it as a ClawHub/plugin experiment for now?
rationale: The requested behavior changes durable skill state, public config, user-data handling, and possible deletion/archive policy, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design a narrow lifecycle API first
options.body: Define the missing failure/outcome/usage signals and persistence contract, then implement only the core pieces plugins or Skill Workshop cannot express.

options.title: Keep it as a ClawHub/plugin experiment
options.body: Ask for an external plugin or bundle-style prototype using current diagnostics and tool hooks, with a follow-up API issue only for proven gaps.

options.title: Decline automatic retirement
options.body: Allow correction-based suggestions to continue but avoid product-owned archive/delete automation until stronger user demand or safety design exists.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow lifecycle API first
recommendation.body: Define the missing failure/outcome/usage signals and persistence contract, then implement only the core pieces plugins or Skill Workshop cannot express.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Skill Workshop suggestion and product-surface work make steipete the strongest current routing candidate for the boundary decision.
